title: German text corrections found during the English translation, November 2026

decision.locator: Chat instruction "You fix the German issues based on your best judgment without my input"
decision.finding: The user asked for the German source issues reported during the English translation to be corrected on the author's judgment.

checks.internal-card-id: Compared the usage note before and after the edit: only the internal card ID(s) were removed and the sentence still reads correctly; each referenced card exists and is still named by its word. Content carried over from the predecessor was not re-reviewed.
checks.dangling-sense-reference: Compared the usage note before and after the edit against the card's meaning line: only the reference to a sense number the card does not show was removed or reworded; the statement it belonged to is unchanged. Content carried over from the predecessor was not re-reviewed.
checks.editorial-jargon: Compared the usage note before and after the edit against the card's aliases: the spelling it mentions is still listed for search, and only the editorial wording was replaced. Content carried over from the predecessor was not re-reviewed.
checks.note-contradicts-example: Read the usage note against all examples of the card: the removed remark described a sentence the card does not contain; the rest of the note is unchanged. Content carried over from the predecessor was not re-reviewed.
checks.factual-correction: Checked the corrected statement against the cited source and re-read the whole note for consistency. Content carried over from the predecessor was not re-reviewed.
checks.unsuitable-example: Read the remaining examples: each is complete, uses the headword in a distinct reviewed context, and the review fields list exactly these sentences. Content carried over from the predecessor was not re-reviewed.
checks.unnatural-example: Checked the new example (Japanese, romanization, German) against the card's meaning, reading and conjugation data, and the reworded note against it; the review fields list the new sentence. Content carried over from the predecessor was not re-reviewed.

corrections.rationale: The usage note dated the official name 児童養護施設 to 1947. The Child Welfare Act of 1947 called these institutions 養護施設; they were renamed 児童養護施設 by the 1997 amendment. The year is corrected and the earlier name added.
noteEdits: in Japan heißen solche Einrichtungen seit 1947 offiziell 児童養護施設 und nehmen
in Japan heißen solche Einrichtungen offiziell 児童養護施設 (so seit der Gesetzesänderung von 1997, davor 養護施設) und nehmen

evidence.source: Japanese Wikipedia, article 児童養護施設
evidence.locator: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%85%90%E7%AB%A5%E9%A4%8A%E8%AD%B7%E6%96%BD%E8%A8%AD
evidence.finding: The article states: 「1997年（平成9年）の児童福祉法改正により、「養護施設」は「児童養護施設」に改称された。」 and 「児童養護施設は、児童福祉法第41条に規定する児童福祉施設である。」 The 1947 act (in force 1948) created the institutional framework; the current name dates from the 1997 amendment. The page does not give the date the amendment took effect, so the note names only the amendment year.

corrections.rationale: The first example was a 100-character anecdote built on a pun (ハゲ症 for 半夏生). It does not show how 夏至 is used, its German translation has to quote romanized Japanese, and as a quiz context it is unusable. It is removed. The two remaining examples cover distinct contexts (the astronomical fact, midsummer festivals abroad).
removeExamples: 父に夏至から11日目のことを何と呼ぶか知っているかと聞かれたので、得意気に「ハゲ症」って答えたんですけど、それって「ハゲ頭の症状」って意味になるみたいで。父は笑って、正しい答えは「半夏生」だよって教えてくれましたけどね。

evidence.source: Nihongo Explorer vocabulary library (German teaching text)
evidence.locator: vocab-n2:1746 examples
evidence.finding: Examples 2 and 3 (夏至は、一年で最も昼が長い日です。 / 北欧では、夏至の日に盛大なお祭りが行われる。) are complete, distinct and already reviewed; the card keeps two reviewed contexts without example 1.

corrections.rationale: The second example used the past form 来たった (ようやく春が来たった). The form follows from the godan conjugation but is practically unused in contemporary Japanese, so the sentence reads as constructed. It is replaced by a sentence with the dictionary form as predicate, the form the note itself cites (時が来たる). The note now says that inflected forms are rare.
noteEdits: Als Verb bezeichnet es das Eintreffen, etwa 時が来たる „die Zeit kommt“. Diese Lesung folgt der Godan-Beugung: きたります, きたった.

Als Verb bezeichnet es das Eintreffen, etwa 時が来たる „die Zeit kommt“; üblich ist dabei fast nur die Grundform, etwa in Titeln und feierlicher Erzählung. Diese Lesung folgt der Godan-Beugung (きたります, きたった), gebeugte Formen sind heute aber selten.

replaceExamples.japanese: 長い冬が終わり、ようやく春が来たった。

with.japanese: 長い冬が終わり、待ちに待った春が来たる。
with.romaji: Nagai fuyu ga owari, machi ni matta haru ga kitaru.
with.german: Der lange Winter geht zu Ende, und der lang ersehnte Frühling hält Einzug.

replaceExamples.context: Elevated narrative arrival of spring with the dictionary form 来たる as predicate; replaces the constructed past form 来たった, which is rare today.
